name: Fintech Organization
description: For fintech companies at any stage where compliance, risk, and regulatory requirements are embedded in every department. Strong regulatory reporting lines with the Head of Compliance/Legal holding a dotted-line relationship to the board. KYC/AML, Fraud, and Payments teams are first-class citizens alongside product teams. Suitable for companies regulated by BaFin, FCA, SEC, or equivalent bodies.

org_structure.overview: Fintech orgs are defined by the tension between speed and safety. The philosophy is 'compliance as a product enabler, not a blocker' — regulatory and risk functions are embedded in product teams rather than isolated in a separate silo that gates releases. The second line of defense (Risk, Compliance, Legal) has independence and authority, including the ability to stop a product launch. The third line (Internal Audit) reports independently to the board audit committee. Key functions unique to fintech include: KYC/AML operations, fraud detection and prevention, payments/financial operations (finops), and regulatory reporting. Technology teams must include deep security architecture and often require dedicated regulatory engineering (RegEng) to build compliance into the platform.

departments.name: Executive & Regulatory Leadership
departments.description: C-suite with regulatory accountability. The CEO often holds a regulated status (e.g., Approved Person under FCA). Direct regulatory reporting lines built into the org.

roles.title: Chief Executive Officer (CEO)
roles.description: Ultimate regulatory accountability. Often a regulated individual under applicable financial services law. Owns the relationship with the primary regulator.

roles.title: Chief Risk Officer (CRO)
roles.description: Owns the enterprise risk management framework, including credit risk, operational risk, liquidity risk, and regulatory risk. Independent from revenue-generating functions.

roles.title: Chief Compliance Officer (CCO)
roles.description: Owns regulatory compliance program, AML/CFT framework, licensing obligations, and regulatory reporting. Dotted line to board.

departments.name: Legal & Compliance
departments.description: Legal advisory, regulatory compliance, and corporate governance. May be separate departments at scale, combined at earlier stages.

roles.title: General Counsel
roles.description: Corporate legal, contracts, IP, regulatory engagement, and litigation management. Advises board on governance.

roles.title: Head of Regulatory Compliance
roles.description: Manages regulatory licensing, compliance monitoring, regulatory change management, and examiner relationships.

roles.title: AML / KYC Officer
roles.description: Owns AML/CFT program, suspicious activity monitoring, KYC procedures, and sanctions screening.

roles.title: Privacy Counsel / Data Protection Officer
roles.description: GDPR/CCPA compliance, data privacy framework, privacy impact assessments, and data subject request handling.

departments.name: Risk Management
departments.description: Independent risk function covering credit, fraud, operational, and liquidity risk. Develops risk appetite framework and monitors adherence.

roles.title: Head of Credit Risk
roles.description: Credit underwriting strategy, credit scoring models, portfolio monitoring, and provisioning (IFRS 9 / CECL).

roles.title: Head of Fraud Risk
roles.description: Fraud detection strategy, fraud modeling, real-time transaction monitoring rules, and investigation team.

roles.title: Fraud Analyst / Investigator
roles.description: Reviews flagged transactions, conducts investigations, files SARs, and tunes fraud detection rules.

roles.title: Operational Risk Manager
roles.description: Risk and control self-assessments (RCSAs), loss event capture, business continuity planning, and third-party risk management.

departments.name: Payments & Financial Operations (FinOps)
departments.description: Owns the payment infrastructure, settlement, reconciliation, treasury, and banking partnerships. Critical for maintaining money transmission licenses.

roles.title: Head of Payments / FinOps
roles.description: Payment operations, scheme relationships (Visa, Mastercard, SEPA, Swift), settlement, and reconciliation.

roles.title: Treasury Manager
roles.description: Liquidity management, bank account structure, payment routing optimization, and FX management.

roles.title: Payments Operations Analyst
roles.description: Daily reconciliation, exception handling, settlement monitoring, and payment failure investigation.

roles.title: Banking Partnerships Manager
roles.description: Manages relationships with sponsor banks, correspondent banks, and payment partners. Leads due diligence and onboarding.

departments.name: Product & Engineering (Fintech)
departments.description: Product teams own customer-facing financial products (payments, lending, cards, investments). Strong security and compliance engineering practices embedded in each squad.

roles.title: VP of Product (Fintech)
roles.description: Product strategy for financial products. Deep understanding of financial regulation and market structure for each product line.

roles.title: Product Manager (Lending / Payments / Cards / Investing)
roles.description: Owns a specific financial product vertical. Must understand applicable regulations (e.g., Truth in Lending, PSD2, MiFID II).

roles.title: VP of Engineering (Fintech)
roles.description: Engineering strategy with emphasis on security, reliability, and auditability. Owns financial infrastructure architecture.

roles.title: Security Engineer / Architect
roles.description: Application security, encryption standards, key management, penetration testing, and secure SDLC.

roles.title: Regulatory Engineering (RegEng) Lead
roles.description: Builds compliance into the platform: automated regulatory reporting, transaction monitoring systems, KYC workflows, and audit trails.

key_relationships: The CRO and CCO have independent reporting lines to the board, not just to the CEO. The board's Risk Committee and Audit Committee provide direct oversight.
Compliance is embedded in product development: every new product feature undergoes a regulatory impact assessment before development begins.
Fraud and Risk teams have real-time access to engineering systems to tune detection rules without being gatekeepers to releases.
Payments/FinOps reconciles daily with the core ledger and reports to Finance — any discrepancy is escalated within 24 hours.
The CRO and CFO jointly review the liquidity position daily, with formal escalation triggers tied to regulatory capital requirements.
Internal Audit reports administratively to the CEO but functionally to the Board Audit Committee — they can audit any department including the CEO's office.
The MLRO (Money Laundering Reporting Officer) has direct access to the board and can file SARs without management approval.
Product Managers are required to complete regulatory training specific to their product area before assuming the role.

Board of Directors
├── Risk Committee (Board)
├── Audit Committee (Board)
└── CEO
    ├── General Counsel / CCO
    │   ├── Head of Regulatory Compliance
    │   │   └── AML/KYC Officer × 1-3
    │   └── Privacy Counsel / DPO
    ├── Chief Risk Officer (CRO) [dotted line to Board]
    │   ├── Head of Credit Risk
    │   ├── Head of Fraud Risk
    │   │   └── Fraud Analyst × 2-8
    │   └── Operational Risk Manager
    ├── CFO
    │   ├── [Standard Finance functions]
    │   └── Head of Payments / FinOps
    │       ├── Treasury Manager
    │       ├── Payments Ops Analyst × 1-3
    │       └── Banking Partnerships Manager
    ├── CPTO / VP Engineering
    │   ├── Security Engineer × 2-5
    │   ├── RegEng Lead
    │   └── [Standard Eng squads]
    └── VP of Product
        └── PM (Lending / Payments / Cards / Investing) × 3-8
